# Results — Study 89 (Turn-of-the-Month) on the real tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The turn-of-month (TOM)
window is **the last trading day of month t-1 through trading day +3 of month t** — the
canonical `[-1, +3]` window (Lakonishok & Smidt 1988). It is **calendar-known** (knowable
in advance), so there is **no execution lag** — a calendar rule is not a forecast (house
rule). The headline runs on the **total-return** SPY tape (dividends folded in, so
buy-and-hold is a fair benchmark); a longer **price-only** `^GSPC` sample is reported
alongside and labelled price-only. Switch cost **5 bps** one-way; cash earns **0%**.
As-of **2026-06-12**; match the fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Series | Mode | Window | Rows | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|--:|---|
| SPY | total return | 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-12 | 8,400 | `eb1569cc9e97` |
| ^GSPC | price-only (no dividends) | 1950-01-03 → 2026-06-12 | 19,233 | `0198a54a32c0` |

## The concentration — TOM window vs rest-of-month

| Tape | TOM mean | Rest mean | Difference | HAC *t* | Window = % of days | …earns % of total return |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **SPY total return (1993–)** | **+7.68 bps/day** | +4.07 bps/day | **+3.61 bps/day** | **+1.17** | 19.1% | **32.9%** |
| ^GSPC price-only (1950–) | +11.02 bps/day | +1.93 bps/day | +9.08 bps/day | **+4.97** | 19.1% | **63.4%** |

> **Gross / price-only labels, explicit:** `^GSPC` carries **no dividends** — it is
> price-only, so its rest-of-month drift is understated and its TOM *share* is flattered
> relative to a total-return series. The headline stamp is the SPY total-return row.

## The TOM-only timer vs buy-and-hold — net of 5 bps/switch (SPY total return)

| Arm | CAGR | Vol | Sharpe (all days) | Sharpe (per-day-invested) | Max drawdown | Time in mkt | Switches |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **TOM-only timer** | **2.20%** | 7.9% | 0.315 | **0.895** | −19.3% | 19% | 803 |
| Buy & hold | **10.82%** | 18.6% | 0.646 | 0.646 | −55.2% | 100% | 0 |

## The decisive numbers

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| TOM-minus-rest daily premium, SPY total return | **+3.61 bps/day, HAC *t* = +1.17** (|t| < 2 — not certified on this tape) |
| Same, long ^GSPC price-only history | **+9.08 bps/day, HAC *t* = +4.97** (certified — but price-only, not total return) |
| Share of total cumulative return earned in the TOM window | **32.9%** (SPY TR) — in **19.1%** of trading days |
| TOM-only timer CAGR vs buy-and-hold | **−8.62 pts/yr** (2.20% vs 10.82%) |
| TOM-only timer Sharpe vs buy-and-hold (whole period) | **−0.331** (0.315 vs 0.646) |
| TOM-only timer Sharpe **per-day-invested** vs buy-and-hold | **+0.249** (0.895 vs 0.646) |
| Decay: early (1993–2009) vs late (2010–) TOM premium | **+5.77 → +1.37 bps/day**; change −4.40 bps, block-bootstrap **p = 0.487** (not significant) |

## How to read it

- **The concentration is real but not "almost all."** In 19% of trading days the TOM
  window earns **33%** of SPY's total-return — a ~1.7x over-representation, striking but a
  long way from the folklore *"almost all the gains."* → 3rd axis **BUSTED** for the
  literal "almost all" claim.
- **Signal is `WEAK` on the tape that matters.** On SPY total-return (1993–) the daily
  TOM-minus-rest premium is **+3.6 bps but HAC *t* = 1.17** — below the bar. The long
  price-only `^GSPC` history *does* clear it (*t* = 4.97), so the literature's effect is
  real over deep history; this modern, dividend-inclusive tape alone can't certify it.
  The early-vs-late contrast points down (5.8 → 1.4 bps) but the difference is **not**
  significant (p = 0.49) — we don't claim "decayed," only "this sample can't certify it."
- **`MIRAGE` as a strategy.** A TOM-only timer earns **2.2%/yr vs 10.8%** — it trails
  buy-and-hold by **8.6 pts/yr** because it forgoes the equity premium the other ~81% of
  the time. Its Sharpe *per-day-invested* (0.895) does beat buy-and-hold's 0.646 — the
  steelman survives **only** after you normalise to per-day-invested — but you cannot bank
  that: holding cash 81% of the time and paying 803 switch-costs leaves you far poorer.
  → Signal **WEAK**, Tradability **MIRAGE**.
